used_by.receivers_nearby: formula: every candidate receiver whose straight-line distance ≤ its type's reach (receiver_radius); each carries its demand (disclosed, else floor area × intensity), the temperature its type needs, its profile, and where the record came from | coef: types: hot-water district network · ambient (low-temperature) network · steam network · pool · ice rink (also a source) · school · hospital or care home · housing · office · greenhouse · wastewater plant. Pools: water ≤ 37 °C by regulation, 25–28 °C recommended for competition pools (BC 2025). Ambient networks (Blatchford) take heat near ground temperature and lift it in each building. Hot water stored for taps must be at least 60 °C, and 49 °C anywhere in a recirculation loop (Vancouver Building By-law 2025 Book II, 2.6.1.12.(1), 2.6.1.1.(3)); so data-centre heat at 25–35 °C can preheat tap water but a heat pump or other source must finish
used_by.backup_neighbours: formula: only behind the data centre's own transfer switch, on a private line, with the utility's written approval; never through the utility's lines | coef: BC: supplying anyone but itself, its employees or tenants makes it a public utility unless the minister (UCA s. 22) or BCUC (s. 88(3)) exempts it; an affiliate is a separate person (2026 BCCA 93, law-firm summary); BC Hydro: never energize a de-energized line. Edmonton: EPCOR bars extending a customer's wiring beyond its property (T&C s. 4.4, exception in Art. 8.3 not yet verified) and islanding without written approval (s. 7.6, 7.8). Spare generator capacity in a blackout is what the data centre's redundancy leaves, not sized here.
